question: In a big cluster of galaxies, where is most of the ordinary matter, the kind made of atoms?
options: In the stars of its galaxies
In hot gas between its galaxies
In cold dust inside its galaxies
answer: In hot gas between the galaxies. At tens of millions of degrees it shines mainly in X-rays, so ordinary photographs miss it, yet in the richest clusters it outweighs the stars several times over. Even so, gas and stars together are a small fraction of a cluster's total mass; most is dark matter.
move: What shows up in the picture depends on the camera, not the world.
trap: Pictures of clusters show galaxies, so the stars seem to be the mass.
source: Sarazin, X-ray Emission from Clusters of Galaxies, 1988
reference: Sarazin, X-ray Emission from Clusters of Galaxies, Cambridge University Press, 1988
